### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.surround, mini.operators

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

In the current implementation, mini.surround prepends `<Cmd> echon ''<CR>` to reset `v:count` to resolve #376. However, this can cause the statusline to disappear when `cmdheight = 0`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c79538ea-fa13-47cb-b6c3-44df53f15bed

Some operators in mini.operators this issue as well. I attempted to find some possible solutions to resolve #376 without leading to this problem:

1. Use `<Cmd>redraw<CR>`, but I'm not sure whether this has inconspicuous side effects.
2. Prepend the proper number of `<Del>`s to reset `v:count`. This method is adopted by [nvim-surround](https://github.com/kylechui/nvim-surround/blob/c271c9082886a24866353764cf96c9d957e95b2b/lua/nvim-surround/init.lua#L65). You can also find some evidence in Neovim's [source code](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/a26cdcb20e68f38f636b14a03c3f9657f5c74f67/src/nvim/normal.c#L916).

I verified both methods, and you can find the changes [here](https://github.com/loichyan/mini.nvim/commit/11a5923f690c5ba1d17e6297106b32dd822f2da8). Personally, I prefer the `<Del>` method, as it seems to have the least potential side effects. This is demonstrated in the video above.

### Reproduction

The minimal configuration to reproduce:

```lua
-- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

-- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
require('mini.deps').setup()

-- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
-- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub

vim.o.showcmdloc = 'statusline'
vim.o.laststatus = 3
vim.o.statusline = 'keystrokes: %S %= %f|%l|%v'
vim.o.cmdheight = 0
require('mini.surround').setup()
```

You can also find this snippet in the [aforementioned link](https://github.com/loichyan/mini.nvim/commit/11a5923f690c5ba1d17e6297106b32dd822f2da8).

Thanks for the issue!

Although `cmdheight=0` is still marked as experimental (as it still has some rough edges, unfortunately), supporting it seems to be not a big of an issue. 

> Some operators in mini.operators this issue as well. I attempted to find some possible solutions to resolve [#376](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/376) without leading to this problem:
> 
>     1. Use `<Cmd>redraw<CR>`, but I'm not sure whether this has inconspicuous side effects.
> 
>     2. Prepend the proper number of `<Del>`s to reset `v:count`. This method is adopted by [nvim-surround](https://github.com/kylechui/nvim-surround/blob/c271c9082886a24866353764cf96c9d957e95b2b/lua/nvim-surround/init.lua#L65). You can also find some evidence in Neovim's [source code](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/a26cdcb20e68f38f636b14a03c3f9657f5c74f67/src/nvim/normal.c#L916).
> 
> 
> I verified both methods, and you can find the changes [here](https://github.com/loichyan/mini.nvim/commit/11a5923f690c5ba1d17e6297106b32dd822f2da8). Personally, I prefer the `<Del>` method, as it seems to have the least potential side effects. This is demonstrated in the video above.

I personally don't like using `<Del>` for whatever reason. Simulating key presses is prone to have unexpected issues. So instead I went the other direction and replaced the `<Cmd>echon ""<CR>` with a direct `<Cmd>redraw<CR>`, as executing *any* commands seems to reset the `[count]`. And extra redraw rarely has crucial side effects when it is done during manual user input (i.e. if it is not automated to be executed on a regular basis).

This should now be resolved on latest `main`.

Sorry for bothering again! I have some new discoveries that may be useful for users who set `cmdheight=0` like me.

First of all, this issue is indeed caused by `cmdheight=0`. Actually, I found that any mapping containing `<Cmd>...<CR>` causes the statusline to disappear. This is true even for an empty `<Cmd><CR>`. This bug can also cause the statusline to flash sometimes, which has bothered me for quite a while =.= Additionaly, on nightly Neovim, if you enable `vim._extui`, this issue never happens.

Another useful fact is that just an empty `<Cmd><CR>` is able to clear `v:count`. So, probably, the only benefit of using `redraw` here is that it can magically keep the statusline on the screen.

> Actually, I found that any mapping containing `<Cmd>...<CR>` causes the statusline to disappear.

Yes, `cmdheight=0` has problems with `<Cmd>...<CR>`. neovim/neovim#20673 was one example and disappear might also be the case.

> Another useful fact is that just an empty `<Cmd><CR>` is able to clear `v:count`. So, probably, the only benefit of using `redraw` here is that it can magically keep the statusline on the screen.

Yes, it does look like it. But working empty `<Cmd><CR>` does feel like intentionally intended behavior and I feel like it can change in the future. So having it with `redraw` should be fine.
